# onpager_team_responder_policy (Resource)

Manage one exact team responder policy importance slot. Control publishes immutable revisions and derives chain snapshots. Destroy resets only this slot while preserving history and existing responder calls. Configure one resource per team and importance; import an existing slot before managing it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_team_responder_policy" "default" {
  team_id    = var.team_id
  importance = "default"
  strategy   = "team_fanout"
}

resource "onpager_escalation_chain" "responders" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "Responder sequence"
  steps = [
    { kind = "notify_user", target_user_id = var.user_id, importance = "important" },
    { kind = "wait", wait_seconds = 60 },
  ]
}

resource "onpager_team_responder_policy" "example" {
  team_id             = var.team_id
  importance          = "important"
  strategy            = "team_chain"
  chain_id            = onpager_escalation_chain.responders.id
  publication_trigger = onpager_escalation_chain.responders.etag
}

variable "team_id" {
  description = "Existing active owning team UUID. Import any configured importance slot before applying."
  type        = string
}

variable "user_id" {
  description = "Existing active team member UUID referenced by the responder chain."
  type        = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `importance` (String) Immutable exact importance slot: `default` or `important`. Explicitly required; no default, fallback or cross-slot ownership. Changing it replaces this resource.
- `strategy` (String) Responder strategy, explicitly `team_fanout` or `team_chain`. Fanout omits chain_id; chain requires an existing owned escalation chain. Publication requires an active team and does not create responder calls or deliver notifications.
- `team_id` (String) Immutable owning team UUID. Required without a default. Changing it replaces this resource. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Optional

- `chain_id` (String) Existing nonzero canonical lowercase escalation-chain UUID. Required only for `team_chain` and must belong to this team. Omit/null for `team_fanout`; empty is invalid. Control derives and saves a canonical immutable snapshot with at least one user/on-call notification and a final wait; channel/webhook steps are unsupported. Later edits to the chain do not change the saved policy until re-publication.
- `publication_trigger` (String) Optional opaque Terraform-only string. A change causes in-place re-publication, for example when set to an escalation chain's `etag`. Null/omitted is valid; empty is a distinct valid value. Preserved across refresh, unavailable/null on import, never sent to Control. This is an explicit re-publication trigger, not an API revision, If-Match value or concurrency guarantee.

### Read-Only

- `chain_steps` (Attributes List) Ordered canonical snapshot returned by Control. Empty [] for fanout. Read-only metadata: configuration cannot supply compatibility steps. A chain retains this snapshot until explicitly re-published; existing responder calls retain their own snapshots. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--chain_steps))
- `id` (String) Stable slot identity and import ID: `team_uuid/default` or `team_uuid/important`.
- `revision` (Number) Observed positive immutable publication revision for this exact slot. A counter only: publication and reset do not send If-Match or use compare-and-swap. Concurrent publications apply in server commit order.

<a id="nestedatt--chain_steps"></a>
### Nested Schema for `chain_steps`

Read-Only:

- `importance` (String) Optional notification importance, default or important. Null when omitted, including canonical waits.
- `kind` (String) Canonical step kind: `wait`, `notify_user`, or `notify_oncall`.
- `schedule_id` (String) Owned schedule UUID for notify_oncall; null for other kinds.
- `target_user_id` (String) Target user UUID for notify_user; null for other kinds.
- `wait_seconds` (Number) Whole seconds for a wait, 1..9223372036. Null for notification steps.

## Import

Import one existing configured slot using `team_uuid/default` or
`team_uuid/important`. Both `team_id` and `importance` are immutable; changing
either replaces the resource. Import and refresh perform only the direct read
of this exact slot. An unconfigured slot cannot be imported as a publication.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_team_responder_policy.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/important"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_team_responder_policy.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/important
```

`publication_trigger` is Terraform-only configuration and is null on import.
Configure it after import when automatic re-publication from a chain reference
is desired. Its first configured value causes an in-place publication.

## Ownership and publication

Configure at most one resource per team and importance. `default` and `important`
are independent slots; one never falls back to the other. Create first reads the
exact slot and refuses an existing publication, even when its contents match.
Import explicitly adopts an existing slot. The provider does not merge or restore
unmanaged policies.

`team_fanout` requires omitted/null `chain_id` and exposes an empty `chain_steps`
list. `team_chain` requires an existing escalation chain owned by this active
team. Its users must be active team members and its schedules must belong to the
team. The API derives the canonical immutable ordered snapshot. Only user and
on-call notifications and waits are supported, with at least one notification
and a final positive wait. Repeat, channel and webhook steps are unsupported.
Wait importance is absent in the canonical snapshot. This resource never sends
the API's compatibility `steps` input, resolves occurrences or discovers targets.

Editing the source chain does not change an already published snapshot. Set
`publication_trigger` to the managed escalation chain's `etag`, as in the example,
to re-publish when that reference changes. Any opaque string, including empty,
is valid; omission/null disables this explicit trigger. Refresh preserves the
saved configured value. The trigger is never sent to the API and provides no
compare-and-swap protection.

`revision` is an observed publication counter. Reads, publications and reset do
not send `If-Match`. Updates publish directly without a pre-write read; concurrent
publications apply in server commit order. The create ownership read is a guard,
not an atomic reservation. Mutations are never retried automatically. Successful
complete publication receipts populate state directly without another read.

## Refresh and destroy

Refresh adopts valid drift within the same exact slot. A complete successful
zero-valued policy response confirms an unconfigured slot and removes it from
state. Authentication, authorization, transport, malformed-response and HTTP
errors, including GET 404, retain state. Failed publication retains prior state.
A confirmed publication with a malformed success receipt preserves the desired
team, importance, strategy, chain and trigger; unverifiable `revision` and
`chain_steps` become null until refresh recovers them.

Destroy issues the supported reset for only this exact importance, with no body
or revision precondition. Repeated reset is a no-op. Cleanup is permitted for
inactive owning teams. Reset preserves policy history, the other importance slot
and existing responder calls with their saved snapshots. A failed reset retains
state. No responder call, delivery, preview or test notification is created by
this resource.

## Permissions

Read, create's ownership guard, import and refresh require team-scoped
`responder_policies.read`. Publication, updates and reset require
`responder_policies.publish` for the owning team. Both support service accounts
with explicit native assignments; token issuance and account ownership grant no
business access. The policy endpoint does not require escalation-chain read
grants for its server-derived snapshot. Managing the separate chain in the
example requires its own documented escalation-chain permissions.
